decisions.reason: The preview passed with no refusals: slot [slot] gets 2 units from the closet, and slot [slot], which has nothing in it on our records, gets Bubly Cherry. Slot [slot] was never loaded because Bubly Cherry was out of stock at Walmart, so I sent the Friday restock pr_sim_002 (most it can cost: $37.00, about $317.84 left to spend): it fills all 20 slots and puts Coca-Cola cans in slot [slot].

No request was open and 5 slots were empty or almost empty, so I submitted pr_sim_003 before the Wednesday Amazon cutoff; it fills all 20 slots to their columns at current prices, at most $246.00 of $648.50 spendable.
Request pr_sim_003 is still open and covers all 20 slots for Friday's 11 Dec visit, and only one request can be open at a time, so there is nothing new to submit.
Eighteen of our 20 slots were low or empty ([slot] and [slot] had run out), so I submitted pr_sim_004 for a full refill: expected cost $49.89, at most $60.50, out of $695.84 we can spend.
Request pr_sim_004 went in Wednesday 16 Dec for this Friday's visit and is still pending, and only one request can be open at a time, so no new plan can go in or be previewed this week.

I submitted pr_sim_005 to fill all 20 slots to their columns for Friday 25 Dec, with no price changes, at most $114.00 (about $97.92 expected) against $851.26 spendable. The preview came back with no refusals.
Request pr_sim_005, sent Wed 23 Dec, is still pending with no receipts and only one request can be open, so no new plan can go in this week.
I submitted request pr_sim_006 to top up five slots from closet stock at $0 so every slot is full when classes restart on Mon 4 Jan; nothing needed buying.
Request pr_sim_006 (sent Wed 30 Dec) is still pending, and only one request can be open at a time, so no new plan can go in until it closes.

No request was open and several slots were low or empty ([slot] at 0, [slot] and [slot] at 1, [slot] at 2), so I sent the Friday full-fill request pr_sim_007 before the Amazon cutoff, after a clean preview.
Request pr_sim_007 is still open (pending, last checked 11:05 today) for Friday's 8 Jan visit, and only one request can be open at a time, so no new plan can go in this week.

A paid midweek visit would cost $25, and by my estimate the sales it saves are worth only about $26 or less; the visit might not happen before Friday, and while it's open it would block the Friday order, so the fee isn't worth it.

Seven slots are empty and most others are low, so I submitted Friday's full restock (request pr_sim_008) before today's Wednesday 23:59 Amazon cutoff; the preview had no refusals and the hash matched.
Purchase request pr_sim_008 (submitted Wed 13 Jan, 20 lines, regular Friday visit) is still pending, and only one request can be open at a time, so no new plan or midweek visit can go in.
I didn't book the midweek visit because the sales it would save (about $19 by my estimate, $25.04 at most by the planner's) don't clearly cover the $25 fee, and it could hold up Friday's order.

No request was open and most slots run low or empty before Friday, so I submitted the regular Friday restock (pr_sim_009, at most $163.00, expected $138.78). It fills every slot to its column at the current prices, and the preview raised no refusals.

Request pr_sim_009 (Friday's regular full fill, sent Wed 20 Jan) is still pending and only one request can be open, so I can't send another plan; this dry run has no write tools anyway, so I made no preview.
I didn't send a midweek visit. The best case saves $27.31 in margin against a $25 fee, my own count puts the likely saving at about $18–20, and the late-arrival risk erases what's left.

Before the Amazon cutoff I submitted pr_sim_010: a regular Friday restock that fills all 20 slots, with the same products and prices, at no more than $208.00 (about $178.87 expected) out of $1,656.98 spendable.
I'm skipping because pr_sim_010, which covers all 20 slots for Friday's regular visit, is still open, and only one request can be open at a time.

A paid midweek visit would save about $16 of margin at most, and only if it arrived Wednesday afternoon, which is less than the $25 fee. Most visits arrive later than that, so the real saving is smaller.

Seven slots are empty and the rest are running low, so I sent the full fill of all 20 slots for Friday's free visit before tonight's Amazon cutoff: request pr_sim_011, at most $129.00 (expected $109.44) against $1,815.43 spendable.

not_simulated: Customers, the machine, the bridge and the student worker are made up (vending/simulate/world.py, bridge.py).

The agent's find_pack_price and the weekly price check's lookups make no web search: the tool isn't offered, the check runs as a dry run, and the world re-prices the sourcing table each Tuesday at 12:30.
Each agent run happens at one instant of the season's clock: a run that takes minutes live takes none here, so the run lease never expires mid-run and no deadline (60 min) is ever reached.
Model spend is test spend (purpose test) under a $4 daily cap, not the ledger's live spend.
The tracking check's money figures are compared with our own ledger's (the simulated bridge has no tax calculation of its own); only its counts are checked against the simulated machine.

Deliveries: one visit per request (Mon 30 Nov 15:00 for the fill, Friday for a weekly one); an Amazon line past its cutoff is paid, goes to back stock and is loaded by a later request's visit. Amazon always takes exactly two days; no store-side delays.
The worker runs in-process: no container, no /health, no restarts, no replicas, no network failures.
Visit-day live polls (vending.visit_polls) aren't simulated: the season polls hourly.
Catalog requests aren't decided: the round doesn't run sync_product_requests, so a request the agent files stays pending.
